name: get-flags
description: Without flagKey: search and browse feature flags; returns a paginated summary per flag (key, name, kind, tags, temporary, archived, deprecated, maintainer, and whether targeting is on) in one environment. Set includeDescription to also return each flag's description. Always set env to the environment the user named. With flagKey: get one flag scoped to env, with the full targeting tree (rules, individual targets, fallthrough, prerequisites) and variations. Each rule and each clause carries an `_id`; pass them as ruleId and clauseId to update-targeting-rules (addValuesToClause, removeValuesFromClause, updateClause) or create-approval-request to edit a clause in place.

env.description: Environment key. Always set to the environment the user named.

expand.description: Only with flagKey. A comma-separated list of fields to expand in the response.

flagKey.description: The feature flag key. Omit to list flags; pass to get one flag.

includeDescription.description: Only without flagKey. Return each flag's description. Off by default.

projectKey.description: The project key

name: create-flag
description: Create a new feature flag in a project. Defaults to a boolean temporary flag. After creation the flag is off in all environments. Multivariate flags require defaults. If the response has needsTeamMaintainer, the flag was not created: ask the user which of the returned teams should own it, then retry with maintainerTeamKey. Set defaults.offVariation to the index of the value your code falls back to, so the new flag behaves like the code while off and needs no approval to stay that way. defaults.onVariation is the index served when targeting is on. To change them later, call update-off-variation (envs ["*"], fallthroughVariationIndex) and update-flag with updateDefaultVariation for new environments.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

name: update-flag
description: Update a flag's top-level settings and variations without changing environment targeting. It takes no environment: names, descriptions, tags, maintainers, and variations are project-wide, so never ask for one. Accepted instruction kinds: updateName, updateDescription, addTags and removeTags (values array), makeFlagTemporary, makeFlagPermanent, updateMaintainerMember, updateMaintainerTeam, addCustomProperties, replaceCustomProperties, removeCustomProperties, updateDefaultVariation, addVariation, updateVariation. updateDefaultVariation takes OnVariationValue and/or OffVariationValue (PascalCase), the variation values themselves, not indexes; for example {"kind":"updateDefaultVariation","OnVariationValue":true,"OffVariationValue":false}. Repeating an addVariation with the same value, name and description is a no-op; the same value with a different name or description is rejected (use updateVariation). Turning a flag on or off is environment-scoped: use toggle-flag, not turnFlagOn or turnFlagOff here. Pass either instructions or variationJsonSchema, never both; make two separate calls.

dryRun.description: If true, the patch will be validated but not persisted. Returns a preview of the flag after the patch is applied.

flagKey.description: The feature flag key. The key identifies the flag in your code.

projectKey.description: The project key

variationJsonSchema.description: JSON schema that replaces the flag's variation schema.

name: toggle-flag
description: Turn a feature flag's targeting on or off in a specific environment.

env.description: Environment key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

name: get-flag-health
description: Get a combined flag health view with lifecycle status, last request time, targeting summary, age, and temporary state. Timestamps in the result are UTC.

projectKey.description: the project key

name: get-flag-status-across-envs
description: Check whether a flag is still evaluated, and where: its lifecycle status (new, active, inactive or launched) and when it was last evaluated. Without env, it covers the project's critical environments when the project has any (the result then has criticalEnvironmentsOnly=true), otherwise every environment. Set allEnvs=true for every environment, for example before cleanup to verify the flag is inactive everywhere. Each environment's `default` is the fallback value the SDK passed when it evaluated the flag, not the value the flag serves; use get-flags with flagKey and env to see what an environment serves.

allEnvs.description: Include every environment instead of only the project's critical environments. Ignored when env is set.

projectKey.description: The project key

name: get-agent-configs
description: Without configKey: search and browse AgentControl Configs (query, tags, view, modes, maintainerId, maintainerTeamKey, sort, limit, offset; filters combine with AND). With configKey: get one config; section is config (default, with variations), health (missing variations, models, prompts, tool references), status (lifecycle across every environment; no env needed), targeting (one environment; requires env), or versions (every saved version of one variation, newest first; requires variationKey). To restore an earlier prompt or model, pass that version's model and messages to update-agent-config resource=variation.

env.description: Required for section=targeting; not used by the other sections.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

section.description: Only with configKey. Defaults to config.

variationKey.description: Required for section=versions; not used by the other sections.

name: create-agent-config
description: Create an AgentControl Config or one of its variations. resource is required. configKey always names the config and variationKey and variationName always name a variation. resource=config creates the config (configKey, name, mode); pass variationKey, variationName, modelConfigKey, modelName, and instructions or messages to also create its first variation, optionally with tools and skills, in the same write. For mode judge, evaluationMetricKey and isInverted are required (isInverted: true if a lower metric value is better). maintainerId (member ID) or maintainerTeamKey (team key) sets the maintainer, not both. resource=variation adds variationKey and variationName to configKey, with model and prompts, or clones sourceVariationKey (omitted model, prompts, tools, skills, and judgeConfiguration are copied from it).

configKey.description: The config's key: the new config (resource=config) or the config to add the variation to (resource=variation).

isInverted.description: True when a lower evaluation metric value is better. False when a higher value is better.

modelConfigKey.description: A model config key from get-ai-model-configs: a global Provider.model-id key such as OpenAI.gpt-4o, or a custom model config's own key.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

resource.description: config: a new config, optionally with its first variation. variation: a new variation on configKey.

skills.description: Agent skills to attach, as {key, version} from get-agent-skills. On update, the array replaces the attached skills; [] detaches them all.

variationKey.description: The new variation's key (resource=config: its first variation).

name: update-agent-config
description: Update an AgentControl Config. resource is required and picks what changes. resource=config: name, description, tags, defaultVariationKey (the variation new environments serve by default; existing environments keep their fallthrough, so change those with resource=targeting), evaluationMetricKey, isInverted, or maintainer (maintainerId or maintainerTeamKey, not both; an empty string removes it). Configs cannot be archived. resource=variation: one variation's name (variationName), model, prompts, tools, or skills, by variationKey. resource=targeting: one environment's targeting, in a single write: on turns targeting on or off; fallthrough sets the default for contexts no rule matches ({"variationKey":"candidate"} serves one variation, {"weights":[{"variationKey":"a","percent":50},{"variationKey":"b","percent":50}]} splits traffic); targetingInstructions changes rules and individual targets with kinds addRule, removeRule, reorderRules, replaceRules, updateRuleDescription, addClauses, removeClauses, addValuesToClause, removeValuesFromClause, updateClause, addTargets, removeTargets, clearTargets, and replaceTargets; rule kinds take ruleId, each kind takes variationKey where it serves a variation, and addTargets and removeTargets also require contextKind (for example user) and values. variation and targeting require confirm=true.

archived.description: Not supported: a config cannot be archived; the tool rejects this field.

confirm.description: Required true for resource=variation and resource=targeting.

env.description: Environment key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

fallthrough.description: The default for contexts no rule matches: {variationKey} serves one variation; {weights, contextKind?, bucketBy?} is a percentage rollout whose percents sum to 100.

isInverted.description: True when a lower evaluation metric value is better. False when a higher value is better.

modelConfigKey.description: A model config key from get-ai-model-configs: a global Provider.model-id key such as OpenAI.gpt-4o, or a custom model config's own key.

on.description: resource=targeting: turn targeting on or off.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

resource.description: config: the config's metadata. variation: one variation. targeting: one environment's on/off, fallthrough, rules, and individual targets.

skills.description: Agent skills to attach, as {key, version} from get-agent-skills. On update, the array replaces the attached skills; [] detaches them all.

targetingInstructions.description: Semantic patch instructions for rules and individual targets. Each instruction or replaceRules rule takes variationKey (a variation key or name) or variationId. addTargets and removeTargets take contextKind, variationKey, and values (context keys), e.g. [{"kind":"addTargets","contextKind":"user","variationKey":"candidate","values":["user-1"]}].

contextKind.description: addTargets and removeTargets: the context kind of values, e.g. user.

name: delete-agent-config
description: Permanently delete an AgentControl Config (resource=config) or one of its variations (resource=variation, with variationKey). Requires confirm=true.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

name: get-ai-tools
description: Without toolKey: list AI tool definitions in a project (limit). With toolKey: get one AI tool definition including its schema. With toolKey and section versions: list that tool's versions newest first, paged by limit and offset; when hasMore is true, pass nextOffset as offset. To attach a tool, put its key and version in a variation's tools array ({key, version}).

offset.description: Only with section=versions. Pass nextOffset from the previous page.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

section.description: Only with toolKey. Defaults to tool. versions pages by limit (1-100, default 25) and offset.

name: create-ai-tool
description: Create an AI tool definition using raw JSON Schema. customParameters is application metadata that is not sent to the model.

customParameters.description: Application metadata, not sent to the model.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

name: get-environment
description: Get a LaunchDarkly environment's client-side ID, mobile key, and approval settings. Use this to initialize a browser or mobile SDK, or to check whether changes need approval: approvalSettings covers flags (required, minNumApprovals, canReviewOwnRequest, canApplyDeclinedChanges) and resourceApprovalSettings covers other kinds such as segment and aiconfig. requiredApprovalTags lists at most 25 tags; requiredApprovalTagCount gives the total when there are more. Does not return the server-side SDK key; use get-sdk-key for that.

environmentKey.description: Environment key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

name: get-sdk-key
description: Return the server-side SDK key (sdk-...) for one environment. This is the only tool that returns that credential. Do not use get-environment, get-projects, get-keys, or get-sdk-active.

environmentKey.description: Environment key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

name: get-projects
description: Without projectKey: list LaunchDarkly projects in the account; use to discover project keys before calling project-scoped toolruntime. To find the project that holds a service's logs, traces or errors, use find-o11y-project instead of matching project names. query searches name or key (case-insensitive), tags filters (all must match), sort is name or -name. If the user named no project, search once with query and ask the user when no single project clearly matches; do not page. Next page: offset + limit. With projectKey: get one project with its environments; use to retrieve environments or verify a project exists. Set fullSettings to true (projectKey only) to also return every project-level setting under a settings object, such as defaultClientSideAvailability, snippet and view-association requirements, the full naming convention, and lifecycle settings (settings.lifecycle: requireReadyToArchive and the checks and day thresholds that decide whether archive-flag is allowed). Neither mode returns server-side SDK keys; use get-sdk-key.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

name: create-project
description: Create a new LaunchDarkly project. Returns the project with its environments, including each environment's client-side ID and mobile key. Does not return server-side SDK keys; use get-sdk-key. Project keys must be lowercase with hyphens, starting with a letter. Production and Test environments are created by default.

name: recommend-flag
description: Record an ADVISORY recommendation on whether a code change should be placed behind a LaunchDarkly feature flag. This tool is READ-ONLY: it does not create, modify, toggle, or delete any flag. Call it exactly once, as the final step, after you have understood the change and explored the surrounding code. The recommendation is what CI parses to post a pull-request check.

recommend.description: true if the change should be released behind a feature flag, false if it should not

verdict.description: The finer-grained outcome. suggested = a new flag is warranted (pairs with recommend: true). reuse-existing = the change should be gated behind an EXISTING flag that already covers this same unreleased feature rather than a new one — set reuse_flag_key (pairs with recommend: true). already-flagged = the change is already protected by a flag in the diff or an off/mid-rollout ancestor gate (recommend: false). not-suited = there is genuinely nothing to flag: pure refactor, docs, tests, dependency bump, or build/CI/tooling change (recommend: false).

reuse_flag_key.description: Set ONLY when verdict is reuse-existing: the key of the existing flag to gate this change behind (the flag that already covers this feature). Omit for every other verdict.

confidence.description: Confidence in the recommendation, calibrated to how clear the signal is and how much surrounding code you verified

risk.description: Optional. Blast radius / severity of the change itself, independent of confidence. low = small additive isolated change; medium = modified business logic / moderate blast radius; high = cross-cutting, API-contract, data-migration, or auth/payments/data-integrity change.

reasons.description: Concise, evidence-based justifications. Each should cite the specific file, symbol, or behavior that drove the verdict.

name: match-release-policies
description: Resolve which release policy governs a flag or proposed tags.

environmentKey.description: Environment key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

name: get-release-policies
description: List release policies and guarded-rollout metric settings.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

name: create-automated-rollout-config
description: Record an automated rollout config for a feature-flagged change. Use it only for AutomatedRollout requests. The guarding flag must already exist. Pass repoFullName, prNumber, and prUrl for the PR the user names or you just filed; omit them when there is none. Each listed environment releases after the merge, pinned in override or by its release policy; to hold one, leave it out (no hold or date field exists). releaseType is only override or policy; immediate, progressive, and guarded are override.releaseMethod values. An immediate release passes only environmentKey, with no releaseType or override. triggerType: flag_eval (default) or webhook, to wait for a CI/CD deploy. Stages have exactly allocation and durationMillis; allocation is thousandths of a percent, so 10% over one hour is {"allocation":10000,"durationMillis":3600000}. override keys are camelCase: releaseMethod, rolloutContextKindKey, stages, metricKeys, rollbackOnRegression. Policy environments can return missing or incomplete policy warnings: surface them in generated comments, do not call the release a clean policy rollout, and do not add tags to make a policy match. Returns config_id, the stored config, and warnings.

endingVariationId.description: Variation a multi-variate flag rolls out to. Boolean flags default to true.

override.description: Inline rollout for releaseType override. Keys are camelCase exactly as named here (releaseMethod, rolloutContextKindKey, stages, metricKeys, metricGroupKeys, rollbackOnRegression), not the snake_case names get-automated-rollout-config returns. For an immediate release, omit override and releaseType and pass only environmentKey.

metricGroupKeys.description: Metric groups that gate a guarded rollout.

metricKeys.description: Metrics that gate a guarded rollout. Guarded needs metricKeys or metricGroupKeys.

releaseMethod.description: immediate turns the flag on and takes no stages or metrics; progressive ramps through stages; guarded ramps through stages gated on metrics.

rollbackOnRegression.description: Roll back automatically when a guarded metric regresses.

rolloutContextKindKey.description: Context kind the rollout allocates by.

stages.description: Required for progressive and guarded. Allocations must be positive and strictly increasing. Guarded caps every stage at 50000 and promotes to 100% after the last stage, so do not add a 100000 stage; progressive usually ends at 100000. Each stage has exactly allocation and durationMillis, e.g. {"allocation":10000,"durationMillis":3600000} for 10% over one hour.

allocation.description: Thousandths of a percent: 100000 is 100%, 10000 is 10%, 1000 is 1%.

durationMillis.description: Monitoring window in milliseconds. Must be greater than 0 for every stage, including the last.

releaseType.description: Only override or policy. override (default) pins the rollout in override; policy waits for the PR merge and the flag's first evaluation, then applies the environment's release policy; it releases on merge and never holds. Do not pass override with policy. immediate, progressive, and guarded are override.releaseMethod values.

triggerType.description: flag_eval (default) starts after the flag is seen evaluating; webhook waits for a CI/CD deploy signal.

waitBeforeReleaseMillis.description: Delay after the preceding environment finishes. Dropped from the first environment, which has nothing to wait after.

executionMode.description: sequential, the only accepted value, releases environments in array order. Omitting it means sequential.

flagKey.description: Key of the guarding flag, which must already exist.

projectKey.description: LaunchDarkly project key.

requiredApplicationKeys.description: SDK-reported application ids that must all evaluate the flag before release, so tests, jobs, and other apps do not trigger it. Pass only ids already instrumented in the repository's SDK configuration; never guess, and omit when there are none. Not a LaunchDarkly application object id.

startingVariationId.description: Variation a multi-variate flag rolls out from. Boolean flags default to false; multi-variate flags need both variation IDs, and setting only one is rejected.

name: get-metrics
description: LaunchDarkly metrics used by experiments and guarded rollouts; for observability metric names in a time window, use get-keys with productType metrics. Without metricKey: list metrics in a project (query, tags, eventKind, isNumeric, hasConnections, maintainerIds, maintainerTeamKey, metricUsedIn, dataSourceKeys, versionIds, sort, limit, offset). With metricKey: get full details for one metric. To find which metric a metric version ID belongs to (experiments reference metrics by version), list with versionIds. Timestamps in the result are UTC.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

sort.description: createdAt, name, connectionCount, or activeConnectionCount. Prefix with - for descending order.

versionIds.description: Metric version IDs. Returns the metrics these versions belong to; each result carries its versionId.

name: create-metric
description: Create a custom, pageview, click, or trace metric. To count each unit's distinct values of a warehouse column, set measureType distinct and name the column in unitAggregationField; valueColumn is only for measureType value. maintainerId sets the maintaining member. eventDefault.value is the number imputed for units that sent no event. This must be 0, and it applies only when disabled=false. When disabled=true, value is not sent. excludeUnitsWithoutEvents still sends eventDefault disabled true with no value. Timestamps in the result are UTC.

denominator.description: Denominator term of a ratio metric; the metric's own event is the numerator term. Custom metrics on a warehouse data source only: requires dataSourceKey.

dataSourceKey.description: Warehouse data source of the denominator term. Omit to use the metric's dataSourceKey.

eventName.description: Event key of the denominator term.

filters.description: Count only events matching context attribute or event property clauses. Custom metrics only. A group joins clauses or further groups with and/or.

measureType.description: distinct counts each unit's unique values of the unitAggregationField column; it does not use valueColumn.

unitAggregationField.description: Required with measureType distinct: the warehouse column whose unique values are counted per unit, for example ORDER_ID.

windowEndOffset.description: End of the measurement window, in milliseconds after the unit's first exposure.

windowStartOffset.description: Start of the measurement window, in milliseconds after the unit's first exposure.

winsorIncludeImputed.description: Count the 0 imputed for units without events when computing the winsorization bounds.

winsorLowerPercentile.description: Clamp unit values below this percentile, in the open interval (0, 100).

winsorUpperPercentile.description: Clamp unit values above this percentile, in the open interval (0, 100).

eventDefault.description: Default for units that sent no event. value is only sent when disabled is false, because Gonfalon omits value when defaulting is disabled. The only supported value is 0; ratio metrics reject any other value.

disabled.description: true leaves units that sent no event out of the analysis.

value.description: Imputed value when disabled is false. Only 0 is supported.

excludeUnitsWithoutEvents.description: Leave units that sent no event out of the analysis instead of counting them as 0.

filters.description: Count only events matching context attribute or event property clauses. Custom metrics only. A group joins clauses or further groups with and/or.

maintainerId.description: The ID of the member who maintains this metric.

measureType.description: distinct counts each unit's unique values of the unitAggregationField column; it does not use valueColumn.

percentile.description: Analyze this percentile of unit values instead of the mean. Requires excludeUnitsWithoutEvents: true.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

traceQuery.description: Trace query of a trace metric, for example service.name = "checkout".

traceValueLocation.description: Where a trace metric with measureType value reads its number, for example duration.

unitAggregationField.description: Required with measureType distinct: the warehouse column whose unique values are counted per unit, for example ORDER_ID.

valueColumn.description: Warehouse column holding the numeric value for measureType value.

windowEndOffset.description: End of the measurement window, in milliseconds after the unit's first exposure.

windowStartOffset.description: Start of the measurement window, in milliseconds after the unit's first exposure.

winsorIncludeImputed.description: Count the 0 imputed for units without events when computing the winsorization bounds.

winsorLowerPercentile.description: Clamp unit values below this percentile, in the open interval (0, 100).

winsorUpperPercentile.description: Clamp unit values above this percentile, in the open interval (0, 100).

name: create-experiment
description: Create a draft experiment on a flag or AgentControl Config. It collects no data until an iteration is explicitly started; return the design for user review before starting. To keep it unstarted, simply do not call a start tool; send only schema properties, with no note or message field. The design (hypothesis, randomizationUnit, metrics, primarySingleMetricKey or primaryFunnelKey, treatments, and flags) goes only inside iteration, never at the top level. Timestamps in the result are UTC.

environmentKey.description: Environment key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

name: start-experiment-iteration
description: Start an experiment iteration and allocate live end-user traffic. Requires explicit user confirmation and must not automatically follow creation or update. Timestamps in the result are UTC.

environmentKey.description: Environment key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

name: get-experiments
description: Without experimentKey: list experiments in a project, optionally filtered by environmentKey, flagKey, or status; each entry has key, name, description, and current iteration status. With experimentKey (environmentKey also required): get one experiment including its treatments, metrics, and current iteration status. Timestamps in the result are UTC.

environmentKey.description: Environment key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.
